title: Every graph is eventually Turán-good and Turán-stable
summary: Let $T_r(n)$ denote the complete $r$-partite graph on $n$ vertices whose part sizes differ by at most one. A graph $H$ is called $K_{r+1}$-Turán-good if, for all sufficiently large $n$, the graph $T_r(n)$ contains the maximum number of copies of $H$ among all $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graphs. We say that $H$ is $K_{r+1}$-Turán-stable if, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $δ>0$ and $n_0$ such that, whenever $n\ge n_0$ and an $n$-vertex $K_{r+1}$-free graph $G$ contains at least $\mathrm{ex}(n,H,K_{r+1})-δn^{v(H)}$ copies of $H$, the edit distance between $G$ and $T_r(n)$ is at most…
